imageUseNotice: Contemporary (`before`), archival (`after`) and `historicalReferences` images are genuine Wikimedia Commons source images, resized and converted to WebP with EXIF removed; they were not generated or AI-restored. Each stop also has one `vision`: an AI reconstruction vision made from an archival photograph, approved by the project owner on 2026-10-15 and always shown labelled as AI with its credit. A vision is not evidence: the archival photographs remain the record. Dates and camera perspectives come from Commons metadata and are caveated where conflicting or approximate.

stops.label: Shortened Apothekenflügel
stops.historicalSummary: The Renaissance Apothekenflügel was begun in 1585 for Elector Johann Georg, attributed to Rochus Graf zu Lynar, and housed the court pharmacy. It was shortened at the end of the 19th century for the new Kaiser-Wilhelm-Straße and bridge (today Karl-Liebknecht-Straße and Liebknechtbrücke); its new end received a historicist Renaissance front. The wing was demolished in September 1950. The circa-1900 Schlossapotheke postcard is a period image after the shortening; it is an archival comparator, not an AI restoration.
stops.perspectiveCaveat: The contemporary image is a broad Spree-side view from/near the Liebknechtbrücke showing the modern Humboldt Forum; it is not documented as an exact south-railing camera position. The mapped stop coordinate is an OSM-derived demo pin, not photo GPS.

stops.label: Historic Schloss Spreefront / Grüner Hut
stops.historicalSummary: The palace's east side was its oldest frontage: it included fabric from the castle founded in 1443, 16th-century Renaissance additions, the Grüner Hut tower and an irregular cluster of wings at the water's edge. The historical state selected here is circa 1900–1939; the palace was demolished in 1950–51. Today's Humboldt Forum has a modern east/Spree façade, unlike the reconstructed Baroque fronts on its other sides. The archival 1903 and circa-1900 sources are period images, not AI restorations.

stops.label: Schinkel Bauakademie
stops.historicalSummary: Karl Friedrich Schinkel's Bauakademie was built in 1832–1836 under Emil Flaminius as a near-square red-brick block with terracotta ornament. It burned out in February 1945, was partly rebuilt, and was demolished in 1962. The contemporary photo shows the still-empty plot with its surviving/reconstructed sample corner; no complete academy is present. The archival photograph is catalogued with DateTimeOriginal 1911 although its filename contains “1888”; preserve that source-date discrepancy. Gaertner's 1868 painting is a separate period depiction, not a photograph.
